name: Maria Cantwell

issue_poll.name: WA Poll (SurveyUSA for KING 5 / Seattle Times / UW CIP), Oct 9–14, 2024; plus Strategies 360 Pulse of Washington, Oct 11–16, 2024
issue_poll.note: Ranks 1–8 from the WA Poll's most-important-issue question (cost of living 27%, democracy 16%, border 12%, abortion 12%, climate 9%, homelessness 6%, crime 5%, guns 5%). Ranks 9–10 are the next issues from the Strategies 360 top-two-issues question that the WA Poll did not list (housing costs 23%, economy/jobs 15%): https://www.strategies360.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/2024-Pulse-of-Washington-S360-Polling-Results-Deck-FINAL.pdf

issues.position: Extend IRA prescription drug savings beyond Medicare
issues.note: H.R.1 exempted orphan drugs from Medicare price negotiation, narrowing it.
Her voting-rights statements found date from 2021–22, not the 2024 campaign.

issues.position: More border security funding; legal path for seasonal farmworkers
issues.note: H.R.1 included large CBP border-security funding; no floor vote on a farmworker visa path.

issues.position: Pass a federal law restoring Roe v. Wade protections
issues.note: No Senate floor vote on codifying Roe found this term.

issues.position: Build infrastructure for a clean-energy transition (no specific policy)
More money to intercept fentanyl at the Mexican border
issues.note: H.R.1 funded CBP drug-interdiction and port inspection scanners; she backed the HALT Fentanyl Act (S.331), which is scheduling, not funding.

issues.position: Expand the low-income housing tax credit
issues.note: H.R.1 raised LIHTC allocations 12% and cut the bond test to 25%; she opposed the package.

issues.position: Bring manufacturing jobs back to the U.S. (direction only)

caveats: H.R.1 decides four issues; her Nay is scored against border, fentanyl and LIHTC funding it contained, as with Hassan's tax rating.
WA Poll field dates (Oct 9–14) inferred from same-poll coverage; the KING 5 issue article does not print them.
She voted Yea on the ROAD to Housing Act (H.R.6644, roll call 182, 2026-06-22), not scored because sources show no LIHTC provisions in it.
